title: Ratatouille
subtitle: Provençal vegetable stew with tomatoes, courgette and aubergine
excerpt: Ratatouille is the great vegetable stew of Provence: aubergine, courgette, pepper, and tomatoes cooked separately and then combined in olive oil and herbs. The key is cooking each vegetable on its own first, so each keeps its texture and flavour rather than collapsing into a mush. A well-made ratatouille is extraordinary -- a poorly made one is grey and watery.
sourceNotes: Ratatouille is the signature summer vegetable dish of Nice and Provence. The name comes from the Niçois term ratatouia (to stir up or mix). The dish is made across Provence but the version associated with Nice and the French Riviera is the most widely known. The technique of cooking vegetables separately before combining is the classic method.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch. Improves over 2 to 3 days.

content.text: Do not skip the step of cooking each vegetable separately. This is what distinguishes a good ratatouille from a vegetable soup. The aubergine goes first -- it takes the longest. Each vegetable is cooked until soft and lightly coloured, then set aside. All the vegetables are combined at the end and simmered briefly in the tomato sauce.

content.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry {{aubergine}} aubergine with a pinch of {{salt-table}} salt for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and golden. Remove. Fry {{courgette}} courgette in 2 more tablespoons of oil for 5 minutes until lightly coloured. Remove. Fry {{pepper-red}} red and {{pepper-yellow}} yellow peppers in 2 more tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes until softened. Remove.

Add {{onion}} onion to the pan with the remaining {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes, {{thyme-fresh}} thyme, and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Return all the vegetables to the pan. Stir gently to combine. Simmer for 10 minutes until the flavours meld and the sauce is thick. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Remove {{thyme-fresh}} thyme and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Scatter {{basil-fresh}} basil over. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The ratatouille is watery and grey
items.cause: The vegetables were not cooked separately, or were added to the tomato sauce raw.
items.fix: Watery ratatouille can be fixed by simmering uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes. Next time, cook each vegetable on its own until golden. This removes the water content. It also concentrates the flavour before the sauce comes together.

content.text: Ratatouille is the summer dish of Provence and the Côte d'Azur. It is made when courgettes, aubergines, and peppers are all ripe in late summer. The dish is eaten warm as a main course, cold as a starter, or at room temperature as an accompaniment to grilled fish or meat. It is also one of the most successful dishes for reheating -- the flavour improves significantly overnight.
